# core/CLAUDE.md — Rust core rules

Applies to everything under `core/`. Build commands and the FFI three-file
lockstep are in the root `CLAUDE.md`; the full design is
`designs/spec/` (§5 the schemas, §6 the op table, §7 the architecture,
§7.10 this module map in the spec's words; its `README.md` is the index). The long form of
each entry below — why the seam fell where it did — is
`designs/adr/core-file-history.md` (the full history of every cut, with its
line counts, is archived; see its "Original" line); this file is what
governs a module now.

## Module map

- `lib.rs` — module declarations and re-exports only. No implementation code.
- `model.rs` — the spec §5.2 SHAPE: the project, its clips, sources,
  actions, markers and nests (a track is `model_track.rs` and the media
  types `model_media.rs`, both re-exported), with
  the serde defaults that say what an absent key means. The struct field
  names ARE the JSON keys. Nothing else lives here but `CanvasOutput`
  (`Canvas.output`, `sdr` or `hlg`, written only when `hlg`, format 23, spec
  §11 HD-2).
- `model_canvas.rs` — `CanvasBlending` (`Canvas.blending`, `encoded` or
  `linear`, written only when `linear`, format 24, spec §11 GR-18, HD-16),
  re-exported by `model.rs`; the recipe canvas carries it only when linear.
- `model_track.rs` — a track (`Track`, spec §5.2's `tracks[]` and a nest's),
  moved out of `model.rs` whole (road map "audio" AP10's toll T1) and
  re-exported by it; the track vocabulary's new keys land here: format 35's
  `volume` (0…`TRACK_VOLUME_MAX`, 4, written only when not 1) and `pan`
  (−1…1, written only when not 0), spec §11 AU-102, and format 36's
  `compressor` and `limiter` (the clip's `model_audio.rs` types, after `pan`,
  written only when set), spec §11 AU-150.
- `model_media.rs` — the media types (`Media`, `MediaOriginal`, `MediaKind`,
  spec §5.2's `media[]`), moved out of `model.rs` whole (road map
  "creator-jobs" CJ0b's toll T2) and re-exported by it, so every
  `crate::model::Media*` path holds; a media record's new keys land here.
- `model_props.rs` — the schema's VOCABULARY: the per-clip property types
  (`VideoProps`, `Crop`, `Shadow`, `ColorAdjust`, `Chroma`, `Filter`,
  `Reflection`, `BlendMode`) and their defaults (the audio group's are
  `model_audio.rs`'s), re-exported whole by `model.rs` so every
  `crate::model::X` path holds. **`BlendMode`'s, `ObscureKind`'s and
  `TrackMatte`'s declaration ORDER are shader discriminants** (`ProjectSnapshot.swift` and
  `TrackMatte.swift` derive the code from the case index, `Compositor.metal`
  compares against the same integers): append,
  never reorder. `Normal` is 0 with no `+1`, so a zeroed uniform block, an
  older recipe and a file with no `blend` key all render source-over.
- `model_audio.rs` — the audio vocabulary: `AudioProps`, `Compressor`,
  `Limiter` (format 30, spec §11 AU-21, written only when set) and `Duck`
  (with format 29's `DuckMode`, `pre_roll`, `hold` and `DUCK_SPEECH_PAD`)
  and `FadeShape` (`fade_in_shape` / `fade_out_shape`, and
  `Transition.audio_shape`), and their defaults, every format-29 key
  written only when not its default, and `AudioProps.isolation` (format
  31, spec §11 AU-50, 0…1, written only when not 0), and format 32's
  `Equalizer` (seven named slots — `HighPass`, `LowShelf`, `EqBand` × 3,
  `HighShelf`, `LowPass` — and `bypass`), `Hum` and `AudioChannels` (spec §11
  AU-31, AU-33, AU-34, each written only when set, `channels` only when not
  `both`), and format 33's `Gate` and `DeEsser` (`audio.gate`,
  `audio.de_esser`, spec §11 AU-43, AU-45, after `channels`, each written only
  when set), and format 34's `Voice` (`audio.voice`, spec §11 AU-140, after
  `de_esser`, written only when set: a `VoiceKind` with no default, an
  `amount` defaulting to `VOICE_DEFAULT_AMOUNT`, an optional `pitch`; its
  ranges in `props_check.rs`, its clamp in `actions_clamp.rs`, the chains
  Swift's), and format 37's `Leveller` (`audio.leveller`, spec §11 AU-66:
  `target_db`, `max_up_db`, `max_down_db`, `response`, after `voice`, written
  only when set; its bounds `audio_dynamics.rs`'s); the FIELD `Clip.audio`
  stays in `model.rs`. Re-exported through
  `model_props.rs`; a pure move out of it (road map "audio" AP0), so the audio
  group's new keys land here.
- `audio_eq.rs` — the EQ's and the hum notch's bounds (format 32, spec §11
  AU-31, AU-33, AU-37): `check_eq` / `check_hum`, run by `props_check.rs`'s
  `check_audio` and refusing in the key's own sentence (`audio.eq.<slot>.frequency
  must be between 20 and 20000, not 5`, a slope that is not 12 or 24, mains not
  50 or 60), and `clamp_eq` / `clamp_hum`, run by `actions_clamp.rs`'s
  `clamp_audio` on an action's end. No sample work; the stage is Swift's.
- `audio_dynamics.rs` — the gate's, the de-esser's and the leveller's bounds
  (format 33, spec §11 AU-43, AU-45, AU-46; format 37, AU-66): `check_gate` /
  `check_de_esser` / `check_leveller`, run by
  `props_check.rs`'s `check_audio` and refusing in the key's own sentence
  (`audio.gate.ratio must be between 1 and 20, not 21`; times through
  `props_check.rs`'s `ticks_in_range`), `check_compressor` /
  `check_limiter` (under a prefix: `audio.` for the clip's, run by
  `check_audio`, and the track's own key for `track_dynamics.rs`, spec §11
  AU-150), and `clamp_gate` / `clamp_de_esser` / `clamp_leveller`
  (each field to its range, NaN to its default), run by `actions_clamp.rs`'s
  `clamp_audio` on an action's end. No sample work; the stages are Swift's.
- `model_text.rs` · `model_shape.rs` · `model_regions.rs` · `model_motion.rs`
  — the text, shape, region and motion vocabularies, each re-exported through
  `model_props.rs`. Text and shape are the two sources the model only
  DESCRIBES and the platform draws and measures: nothing in either file is
  ever a measured size. Regions (`Spotlight`, `ObscureRegion`, `SpotShape`,
  `MAX_OBSCURE`) share one coordinate frame — the centre as an offset in
  SOURCE pixels from the centre of the layer's cropped rect — which
  `edit_zoom.rs` writes out as an equation and nothing else restates. The
  one load-bearing declaration order in these four is `ObscureKind`'s
  (`model_regions.rs`), a shader discriminant like `BlendMode`'s above;
  elsewhere only the JSON spelling of every variant is, so a rename needs a migration step. The enums are closed:
  there is no neutral kind to fall back to.
- `model_words.rs` — the word-caption vocabulary (format version 9, road
  map 8's W1b): `TextCase`, `Word`, `WordMode`, `ActivePill` and
  `WordStyle` (whose `template()` is what `patch.rs`'s text template walks
  against), re-exported through `model_props.rs`; the FIELDS (`case`,
  `words`, `word_style`) close `TextProps`. Format version 12 (spec §11
  W-12) added three looks as KEYS, each off by default: `ActivePill.glide`,
  `WordStyle.active_fill` and `WordStyle.pause_dim` (0–1, range-checked in
  `props_check.rs`); `Word.end` is read by the recipe since then, not only
  by the pager. It also holds the two facts
  every writer of `text.words` shares, both `pub(crate)` and so named
  directly by their callers (a glob re-export cannot widen them):
  `token_count`, THE token rule (`split_whitespace` — the core is the one
  counter, spec §11 W-2), and `rebase_words`, the one saturating
  subtraction `trim_start`, `roll`, `add_transition`'s handle form and
  `split`'s second half make (W-3). Word times are clip-time POSITIONS: a
  negative start is legal, equal starts are legal, and `snap_animation`
  puts them on the grid after `check_text` has named what the caller sent.
- `model_graphic.rs` — the graphic vocabulary (format version 10, road
  map 10): `GraphicProps` (`name`, `width`, `height`, `in`, `length`,
  `props`) and `GRAPHIC_MIN_SIDE` / `GRAPHIC_MAX_SIDE` and the schema limits
  `GRAPHIC_MAX_PROPS` / `GRAPHIC_MAX_OPTIONS` / `GRAPHIC_MAX_STRING` /
  `GRAPHIC_TYPES` (`GRAPHIC_MAX_SIDE` restates the engine's `MAX_SIDE` and the
  header's `RC_GRAPHIC_MAX_SIDE`, and each other `GRAPHIC_<X>` the engine's
  `<X>`; `tests/graphic_ffi.rs`'s
  `one_max_side_in_the_engine_the_core_and_the_header` and its four
  `one_…_in_the_engine_and_the_core` tests pin them),
  re-exported through `model_props.rs`; the FIELD `Clip.graphic` stays in
  `model.rs`. And the `pub(crate)` checks every writer shares: `check_name`
  (G-3's `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{0,62}$`, its clause `NAME_RULE` shared with
  `validate`), `check_side`, `check_schema` (the engine's sentences, COPIED —
  no module of the model may name the crate, G-2; a non-boolean `animate`
  on an entry is refused, G-41), `check_props` (by dotted
  path against the schema the op carries, shape only without one; a `null`
  is a removal and is never checked), `check_typed` (one value against its
  entry, answered normalised; `edit_action_graphic.rs` calls it under
  `graphic.props.<key>`), `check_count` (on the map about to be
  STORED). **A props map is changed only by `insert` and
  `shift_remove`**: under `preserve_order`, `Map::remove` is `swap_remove`,
  and `Project ==` cannot see the reorder.
- `model_look.rs` — the look vocabulary (spec §11 GR-7): `Look {kind, amount}`
  (the FIELD `VideoProps.look`, optional, written only when set) and the eight
  built-in looks' definitions as data — Color's four, Light's nine and a split
  tone each — which the recipe's `look` key carries whole, so retuning a look
  is a core change only. `actions.rs` turns a merged look with no valid `kind`
  into `null`, so an action's end can never drop the clip's video group.
  `kind: "lut"` names an imported LUT's media (`media`); `BUILT_IN` is the
  eight. `actions.rs`'s object discriminants (`kind`, `media`) switch at an
  action's end instead of interpolating.
- `model_grade.rs` — tier 2's grading vocabulary (format 16, spec §11 GR-11): `Wheels {lift,
  gamma, gain}`, each a `Wheel {x, y, master}`, the FIELD `VideoProps.wheels` written only when
  not neutral and each key only when not 0; `actions::wheels_json` writes all nine for the
  evaluator, the patch template and the recipe, as `color_json` does tone's. Format 17 (GR-12)
  adds `Curves {master, red, green, blue}`, each an optional list of 2–16 `[x, y]` points
  (`CurvePoint`), the FIELD `VideoProps.curves` written only when not the identity
  (`curve_is_identity`: every y = x, from x 0 to x 1); format 20 (GR-32) adds `hue_hue` and
  `hue_sat` (`[hue, value]` points, 0 ≤ hue < 360) and `CurveDomain` (each channel's identity,
  neutral and value range; `named()` and `named_mut()` give each channel's), a hue curve the
  identity when every value is its neutral; `actions_curves.rs`'s `curves_json` writes all
  six, an absent one as its domain's identity. Format 18 (GR-13) adds `Qualifier {hue,
  saturation, luma, invert}` (`HueRange {center, width, softness}` in degrees, `LevelRange
  {low, high, softness}` 0–1, a range `None` when off), the FIELD `VideoProps.qualifier`,
  written only when not neutral; it acts only on an adjustment clip. Format 21 (GR-35)
  adds `Qualifier.blur` (0…1, written only when above 0, after `invert`) and
  `QUALIFIER_BLUR_MAX`; `is_neutral` counts it, so a blur alone is kept. Re-exported whole
  by `model_props.rs`.
- `cube.rs` — the `.cube` reader (spec §11 GR-8): 3D only, size 2–65, the
  default domain; anything else refused by line and name. `ffi_cube.rs` — the
  four `rc_cube_*` exports. `lut.rs` — a LUT media's rules: placing one is
  refused, removing one clears the looks that name it (the clips stay) and
  the Camera Log of the media it converts, refusing first without
  `with_clips`; paste carries it by path. `Project::check_lut_reference` is
  the one check of a LUT named by media id, keyed by its field
  (`video.look.media`, `color.lut`).
- `cursor_file.rs` — the cursor file, format v1 (road map "creator-jobs" CU1a, spec
  §11 CU-10): its module doc IS the format's specification (the header, the columns
  in integer µs and points × 100, the caps, every refusal's sentence, the parse
  order); `RC_CURSOR_FILE_VERSION` (the header's `#define` held to it by
  `core/tests/cursor_file.rs`), the caps, the types and `CursorFile::parse`, which
  reads the object, `format`, `version` and CU-7's `typed` keys loosely BEFORE the
  strict `deny_unknown_fields` read through `serde_path_to_error`, so a newer file is
  refused by its version and a project by its format. `cursor_file_check.rs` — its
  check (`check`, `check_typed`; a shortcut holds `cmd` or `ctrl`, or `opt` with
  `OPTION_SHORTCUT_KEYS`, CU-60) and the base64 decoder, a module of its own because
  the two together pass the 400-line cap for a new file. `ffi_cursor.rs` —
  `rc_cursor_open` (parse and check; an open is the recorder's read-back, CU-15),
  `rc_cursor_free` and `rc_cursor_query` (road map creator-jobs CU2, spec §11 CU-25).
  `cursor_track.rs` — `CursorTrack`, the handle: the parsed file and its prepared
  paths under a `Mutex` (a `state` holds it only to clone an `Arc`, a poisoned lock
  taken with `into_inner`), ticks ↔ µs through `time.rs`, CU-20's M2 mapping per
  geometry entry (`scale_factor`, not `pixels_per_point`; `to_movie`, the one function), the raw path, idle opacity (CU-22),
  the image in force and ripples (CU-23). `cursor_smooth.rs` — `hold_end`, the one
  hold rule, and `SmoothPath` (pins, RDP, centripetal Catmull–Rom; CU-21).
  `cursor_query.rs` — the request vocabulary (its module doc) and `query`.
  `cursor_query_reads.rs` — its `events` and `path` reads, a pure move out of it (road map
  creator-jobs CU11a's toll); `state` takes `ends` and answers the shutter's two positions (spec
  §11 CU-115).
  `cursor_bursts.rs` — typing stretches and scroll bursts, one run finder. Auto Zoom's
  planner (road map creator-jobs CU7, spec §11 CU-70…CU-75), `plan_zooms` in
  `rc_cursor_query` (one track per clip, and the project): `cursor_zoom.rs` its
  arguments, refusals in CU-75's order, Replace's removals (`is_zoom` only), the bases a
  hold across a cut sets, and the ops (`remove_action`, `set_video`, `add_zoom_action` in
  time order) and answer; `cursor_zoom_run.rs` a run (clips continuing one source on one
  track) — its anchors through S, scroll bursts, barriers, the 10 Hz follow cursor and
  `land` (only given clips, no straddled cut); `cursor_zoom_visits.rs` anchors → visits →
  planned actions in container time, pure. Add Shortcut Overlays' planner (road map
  creator-jobs CU8, spec §11 CU-80…CU-84), `plan_overlays` in `rc_cursor_query` (one track per
  clip, and the project): `cursor_overlays.rs` — its arguments and refusals, the presses through
  `cursor_zoom_run.rs`'s `media_in` and `clip_time`, CU-80's timing in grid frames
  (`min_frames`, D_min(n) = 10n + 25; the same chord merged as "×k"; a different chord more than
  0.5 s late dropped), CU-83's Shortcuts track rule (`TRACK_NAME`; the front-most one in front of
  every given clip's track, unlocked, shown, no matte, free over the span, else a new one at the
  front with `next_id`) and the `add_track` / `add_graphic_clip` ops. Speed Up Typing's
  planner (road map creator-jobs CU9b, spec §11 CU-91, CU-92), `plan_typing` in
  `rc_cursor_query` (one track per clip, and the project): `cursor_typing.rs` — its arguments
  and refusals (rate ×2–×8, shortest 1–30 s, then per clip; reversed refused), each typing
  stretch clamped to the played window through `clip_time`, less every speech span of a media
  clip with sound under it (`speech_in_clip`) and each recorded press's overlay span
  (Shortcuts-track clips holding it or starting within `MOST_LATE`, else `DEFAULT_DURATION`,
  both `cursor_overlays.rs`'s; presses not filtered by `[from, to)`), every clip's pieces
  united (touching merged) before `shortest` and the 0.3 s margins, `needs_speech` when a
  counted media has no `speech`, and the `retime_range` ops right to left, tried in order on a
  clone (all or nothing). `encode_base64`
  sits beside `decode_base64` in `cursor_file_check.rs`, base64's one home. No file
  I/O, no pixel work: a PNG is checked by its signature.
- `model_cursor.rs` · `cursor_props.rs` · `recipe_cursor.rs` — the cursor in the model and the
  recipe (format 38, road map "creator-jobs" CU3a1, spec §11 CU-30, CU-32, CU-35, CU-39):
  `model_cursor.rs` `MediaCursor` (`media.cursor`, after `speech`, written only when set,
  `in_picture` required) and `CursorProps` (`video.cursor`, after `look`, written only when set,
  every field written, `{}` the defaults) with `CursorStyle`, `CursorClicks` and the `CURSOR_*`
  ranges, re-exported through `model_props.rs`; `cursor_props.rs` `check_cursor` (one line in
  `props_check.rs`'s `check_video`), `clamp_cursor` (one line in `actions_clamp.rs`'s
  `clamp_video`; it never fails, so the video group always decodes), `check_media_cursor`

## Rules

**Modules and size.** New feature area = new module with its own
`impl Project` block. Soft cap ~600 lines; needing a new `// ---- name --`
banner section is the signal to split. Every module keeps a `//!` doc;
numeric and algorithmic choices get prose "why" comments. **A file at the cap
gives something up BEFORE it takes anything on**: the cut is a PURE MOVE,
landed and gated alone, so the feature's diff is attributable; budget the cut
against the pessimistic number, because an estimate here has run about two
thirds of the truth. Over the cap today and known debt, not licence:
`edit.rs`, whose
standing exemption is that its module doc IS the op table's semantics half
(the cut there, if ever forced, is the `Op` enum into an `edit_ops.rs`, and
never in the same phase as a feature). The current list is `wc -l`; named
seams are in `designs/adr/core-file-history.md` "Named next cuts".

**Dependencies.** `serde` and `serde_json` (the JSON the FFI speaks),
`tiny_http` (the agent's socket), and `serde_path_to_error`, which is there
so a patch refusal names the path to what only the type can refuse (a
misspelt variant, a `null` a required field cannot take), where serde alone
names only the value. `graphic` (the path crate `../graphic`, road map
10's motion-graphics engine), named by `ffi_graphic.rs` alone. It enables
`serde_json`'s `preserve_order`, and a feature is unified across a path
dependency, so the core's `serde_json` has it too; `Cargo.toml` spells it
out. `svgtypes` 0.16.1 (usvg's own pin, already in the lock) for its
named-colour table only, so a stored name agrees with what usvg draws
(`model_color.rs`). `sha2` for the `.fjgraphic` manifest's checksums
(G-46; also `graphic_ffi.rs`'s revision oracle).

**One implementation per algorithm.** Before writing time math, find the
existing implementation and route through it. Shared constants have exactly
one home (`TIMESCALE` in `time.rs`; `RC_*` caps in `format.rs`; the
inspector's bounds in `props_check.rs`).

**Purity.** Every edit takes `&self` and returns a new value — internally
clone-then-mutate. An op that would change nothing returns
`Outcome::Identity`, never an identical copy: an identical copy registers a
phantom undo step in the app.

**Errors.** Every edit answers `Result<Outcome, String>` — three arms and
one tier, no error enum. `Outcome::Applied` = the new project;
`Outcome::Identity` = the op is valid and nothing needed to change;
`Outcome::Refused(String)` = a rule declined it, carrying the rule's OWN
sentence rather than a second one written at the call site; `Err(String)` =
invalid arguments, unknown ids, parse failures — lowercase messages naming
the offending value. A refusal is not an error tier: both middle arms leave
the project untouched and register no undo step. No input may panic. FFI
mapping (`ffi_edit.rs`): `Applied` → a new handle; `Identity` → NULL with
neither channel written; `Refused` → NULL with the sentence through
`reason_out`; `Err` → NULL with the message through `err_out`; caught panic
→ `"internal error: <what>"`. The two channels are never both written.

**Times.** Every tick value that reaches the model is snapped to the
document's frame grid before it is stored (`time::snap_to_frame`). Never
store a sub-frame time. Where a range check names the value, the check runs
on what the CALLER sent and the snap follows it, so a refusal never names a
number the door rounded to (`props_check.rs`, `edit_props.rs`'s
`snap_motion` / `snap_animation`). The one family that is deliberately NOT
on the grid is the audio ramps — `audio.fade_in` / `fade_out`, the duck's
and the compressor's attack and release — because they are envelope lengths
sampled at the audio rate, not positions in the picture, and quantising them
to a video frame would round a 10 ms attack to nothing. The other is a SHIFT
(spec §11 #42): an op that moves several clips — the ripples, `close_gap`,
`insert_time`, `move_clip` — moves them all by ONE delta so abutments stay
exact, and at a rate whose frame is not a whole number of ticks (7 fps) a
moved start may sit a tick off the grid; a canvas rate change re-snaps (D7-3).

**FFI exports.** Every export: `#[no_mangle] pub unsafe extern "C"`, a `///`
comment restating the header contract, a `/// # Safety` paragraph, NULL
tolerance first, narrow `unsafe {}` blocks. Route through the shared helpers
in `ffi_util.rs` — a freshly hand-rolled `catch_unwind` is a review flag.
Export names mirror the Rust method exactly.

**Format changes.** Any change to persisted project state bumps
`RC_FORMAT_VERSION` in `format.rs` **and** the `#define` in
`core/include/framejob_core.h`; the reader must keep accepting every prior
version; the writer enforces the reader's caps. A bump whose new fields all
carry a serde default needs no migrate step (versions 3 through 15 have none;
15's one step only renumbers the branch's 1015)
but still bumps, because unknown keys are ignored at every level by design
and an older build would otherwise open the file, drop the new fields on read
and write the loss back on the next save; a bump that changes a field's
SHAPE adds a step at the migration hook (`migrate_1_to_2`). Each bump gets a
`schema_vN.rs` test that opens the previous versions' fixtures and reads the
new keys' ORDER off the written text, since a parsed `Value` sorts them.
**Nothing that checks the version writes the current number as a
literal**, so a bump edits `format.rs` (and `format_history.rs`'s paragraph)
and the header and no test or proof:
- The "one past the current version, refused" tests in
  `core/tests/schema_v3.rs` and `core/tests/model_tests.rs` compute
  `RC_FORMAT_VERSION + 1` and assert the refusal's whole message with
  both numbers.
- `schema_v3.rs`'s `the_header_states_the_same_format_version_as_the_core`
  holds the header's `#define` to `format.rs`'s constant, so a bump that
  moves only one of them fails `make test`.
- The schema tests' and `model_tests.rs`'s `/version` assertions read
  `RC_FORMAT_VERSION`; `schema_v10.rs`'s byte-for-byte round trips rewrite
  the fixture's version line through its `current()` helper.
- The proof scripts (`tools/proof/*_proof.py`) read the HEADER's number
  through a `format_version()` helper. `phase9`'s "one past" fixture is
  `format_version() + 1`, and its every-version loop runs up to the current
  version. A proof that expected a literal would fail weeks later, in
  someone else's session, with nothing pointing at the bump.

A fixture's own version (`e2_proof.py`'s `VERSION = 8`, a
`schema_vN.rs`'s older files) is a literal on purpose. One claim still
moves with the schema rather than the number: when a bump appends a key to
the video object, `schema_v4.rs`'s text assertion about what follows
`obscure` fails in `make test` and names the new neighbour.

**Tests.** All tests are black-box in `core/tests/` (no `#[cfg(test)]` in
`src/`), exercised **through the FFI** wherever possible, and verified

**Frozen files.** `EditorViewController.swift`, `TimelineView.swift`,
`PreviewCanvasView.swift`, `AgentServer.swift` are **frozen at current
size**: anything adding more than ~50 lines goes in an extension file
(`EditorViewController+<Feature>.swift`, `TimelineView+<Feature>.swift`,
`AgentServer+<Feature>.swift`) or a new `…SheetController`, and the frozen
file keeps only the wiring — a stored property, a closure assignment, a
validator arm, a draw call. The pieces extension files build on are therefore
internal, not private. Pitfalls: a selector declared `@objc` on an extension
needs NO forward in the frozen file (a second declaration is an error); a
command whose body sits at the foot of a non-extension feature file carries
its validator arm there too, or the item falls through to the closing
`return true`; `handleEditorCharacter`'s bare-key `switch` matches in SOURCE
order, so a bare `case "x"` goes BELOW any modified `case "x" where …`; and
`handleEditorKey` refuses while a sheet is attached, because a sheet is
window-modal and the preview panel's forwarded keys would otherwise reach
the key map behind it.

def slugify(text):
    """A heading's anchor, as Starlight makes it (github-slugger)."""
    text = re.sub(r"<[^>]+>", "", text)
    text = re.sub(r"\[([^\]]*)\]\([^)]*\)", r"\1", text)
    text = text.replace("`", "").replace("*", "").strip().lower()
    text = re.sub(r"[^\w\- ]", "", text)
    return text.replace(" ", "-")


def anchors(text):
    """Every anchor a page has: its headings, numbered as repeats are, and any explicit id."""
    body = FENCE.sub("", split_page(text)[1])
    seen, found = {}, set()
    for heading in re.findall(r"^#{2,6}\s+(.+?)\s*$", body, re.M):
        slug = slugify(heading)
        count = seen.get(slug, 0)
        seen[slug] = count + 1
        found.add(slug if count == 0 else f"{slug}-{count}")
    found.update(re.findall(r"""\bid=["']([^"']+)["']""", body))
    return found


def headings(text):
    return {slugify(heading) for heading in
            re.findall(r"^#{2,6}\s+(.+?)\s*$", FENCE.sub("", split_page(text)[1]), re.M)}

---
title: "Export: start, then poll"
description: Write a file from an agent, follow the job until it finishes, stop it, and read what the file holds.
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

An agent's export doesn't wait for the file. `export` checks the request, puts a job on the Export Queue and answers at once, and the agent then asks how it's going until it ends.

<AtAGlance
  menu={['File ▸ Export…', 'Window ▸ Export Queue']}
  keys="⌘E"
  where="The export sheet's Add to Queue, and each row's Cancel in the Export Queue"
  tools={['export', 'export_status', 'cancel_export']}
/>

## Write a file

<Steps>

1. Call `export` with a preset and a path. It answers straight away.

   ```json
   { "preset": "h264", "path": "~/Movies/cut.mp4", "size": "1080p" }
   ```

   ```json
   { "export_id": 3, "path": "/Users/you/Movies/cut.mp4", "status": "running" }
   ```

2. Call `export_status` with that `export_id`, pause, and call it again until `status` is `done`, `failed` or `cancelled`.

3. Read the `done` answer. It says what the file holds, including the loudness it measured and any warnings.

</Steps>

To stop the job, call `cancel_export`. The job shows in **Window ▸ Export Queue** like any other, but the window doesn't open by itself.

## Export

`export` does what **File ▸ Export…** does with **Add to Queue**, and it runs through the same writer, so an agent's file and a person's match. It takes the [export sheet](/export/export-sheet/)'s controls in the sheet's own terms, apart from the frame rate.

| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `preset` | string | Yes | The encoding: a container and a codec. See [Presets](#presets). |
| `path` | string | Yes | Where to write, such as `~/Movies/cut.mp4`. See [Path handling](#path-handling). |
| `size` | string or `[width, height]` | No | The output size. See [Size](#size). |
| `range` | string | No | `project` for the whole timeline, or `in_out` for the in and out range. See [Range](#range). |
| `video_bitrate` | integer | No | Target video rate in bits per second. See [Exact bitrates](#exact-bitrates). |
| `audio_bitrate` | integer | No | Target AAC or Opus rate in bits per second. See [Exact bitrates](#exact-bitrates). |
| `loudness_lufs` | number | No | Normalise the whole mix to this loudness, −70 to 0. See [The loudness report](#the-loudness-report). |
| `peak_dbtp` | number | No | The master limiter's ceiling, −20 to 0. See [Peak dBTP](#peak-dbtp). |
| `audio_bits` | integer | No | 16 or 24, for WAV and AIFF. See [Audio bits](#audio-bits). |
| `stems` | string | No | `tracks` or `names`, to write stems beside an audio mix. See [Stems](#stems). |
| `burn_in_timecode` | boolean | No | Draw the project timecode over the picture, on top of everything. Off by default. See [Burn in timecode](/export/burn-in-timecode/). |
| `dynamic_range` | string | No | `hlg`, `pq` or `sdr`, in an HLG project. See [Dynamic range](#dynamic-range). |
| `encoder_speed` | string | No | `faster`, `balanced` or `smaller`, for AV1. See [Encoder speed](#encoder-speed). |
| `project` | string | No | The path of the open project to export, as `get_project` reports it. Without it, the frontmost project. |

It answers `{export_id, path, status}`. `path` is the file that will be written, with `~` expanded and the extension corrected. `status` is `running` if the job started at once, or `queued` if it's waiting.

Exports run one at a time, behind anything already in the queue. A job writes the project as it stood when `export` was called, so later edits don't reach it. Calling `export` pauses playback in that project's window.

`export` takes no `scope`. With a [nest](/mcp/nests/) open it still writes the project's timeline, not the nest's.

## Export status

`export_status` answers how a job is going, as its row in the Export Queue would, and it never waits. Pass the `export_id`, which is an integer of 1 or more.

Every answer carries `export_id`, `status`, `path` and `elapsed`, the seconds since `export` was called, or from then to the finish once the job has ended. The rest depends on the status.

| `status` | Also carries |
| --- | --- |
| `queued` | `waiting` while an AV1 or VP9 job is held for memory. `estimated_seconds` on `av1`, `av1_webm`, `vp9_webm` and `vp9_alpha_webm`. |
| `running` | `progress`, from 0 to 1. `phase` while the export names one, which is "Measuring loudness…" during the first pass over the mix. `estimated_seconds` on the same four presets. |
| `done` | What the file holds, in the next table. |
| `failed` | `reason`, the queue row's sentence. |
| `cancelled` | `reason`, the queue row's sentence. |

`estimated_seconds` is the export sheet's estimate of the whole export in whole seconds, and it's only an estimate.

`waiting` is a sentence such as "Waiting for memory: AV1 and VP9 exports running now hold about 2.1 GB of the 8.0 GB this Mac allows them, and this one needs about 7.0 GB." AV1 and VP9 exports may hold a quarter of this Mac's memory between them. While one is held, a later job in the queue may run first.

A `done` answer adds these keys.

| Key | What it holds |
| --- | --- |
| `ok` | `true`. |
| `bytes` | The file's size. |
| `preset`, `container`, `codec` | What was written. |
| `width`, `height` | The file's size in pixels. These are reported on audio presets too, where they mean nothing. |
| `fps` | The rate as `[num, den]`, such as `[30, 1]`. |
| `start`, `duration` | The part of the timeline written, in [ticks](/mcp/units-and-ids/). |
| `burn_in_timecode` | Whether the argument was on. |
| `dynamic_range` | The picture written: `hlg`, `pq` or `sdr`. Only for a video preset in an HLG project. |
| `encoder_speed` | The speed used. Only on `av1` and `av1_webm`. |
| `audio_bits` | The depth written. Only on `audio_wav` and `audio_aiff`. |
| `stems` | `[{name, tracks, path}]`, one per file beside the mix. Only when `stems` was asked for. |
| `loudness` | What the mix measured. See [The loudness report](#the-loudness-report). |
| `graphic_warnings` | `[{name, frame, message}]`, each distinct warning a graphic gave while the file was drawn, up to 64. `frame` is the graphic's own frame, or `null`. Absent when there were none. |
| `cursor_warnings` | `[{media, path, message}]`, each media whose cursor file couldn't be drawn. Its clips were written without a cursor. Absent when there were none. |

## Cancel export

`cancel_export` stops a job, as the row's **Cancel** does, and answers as `export_status` does. Pass the `export_id`.

| The job is | What happens |
| --- | --- |
| Queued | It's cancelled before it starts. The answer reads `cancelled`, with the reason "Cancelled before it started." |
| Running | It stops and its half-written file is removed. The answer may still read `running` until the writer has stopped, and `export_status` then reads `cancelled`, with the reason "Cancelled." |
| Finished | It's left alone, and its file stays. The answer is the finished job's. |

## Export id and its lifetime

An `export_id` is known until Frame Job quits. Removing a finished row from the Export Queue, or choosing **Clear Finished**, doesn't lose it, so an agent can still read how that job ended.

Only ids that `export` answered are known. A job a person queued from the sheet has no id an agent can follow. Any other number answers "No export this launch has export_id 7 — ids come from export and last until Frame Job quits."

## Refusals and failures

A problem Frame Job can see from the request comes back from `export` itself as an error, and nothing is queued.

| The request | What stops it |
| --- | --- |
| An empty timeline | "There is nothing on the timeline to export." |
| A folder that doesn't exist | "There is no folder at … to write into." Frame Job never creates the folder. |
| An unknown preset | The error lists all the presets. |
| An unknown `size`, or one it can't read | The error lists the sizes. See [Size](#size). |
| `range` of `in_out` with no range set | "This project has no in/out range — set one with set_range `{start, end}`, or export with range \"project\"." |
| A number out of range, or a word it doesn't know | The error names the argument and the value. |
| An option the preset doesn't have | See [Audio bits](#audio-bits), [Stems](#stems), [Dynamic range](#dynamic-range) and [Encoder speed](#encoder-speed). |
| A graphic clip in the range with no module, or a module that doesn't compile | "The export was not started: the graphic "…" does not compile — …. Fix the module and export again." It names each graphic and its first error, and it covers graphics inside nests. An audio-only preset draws no graphics, so it isn't stopped by one. |

Anything that goes wrong after that comes back from `export_status` as `failed`, with the sentence in `reason`. Check for it even when `export` answered cleanly.

| What went wrong | The `reason` |
| --- | --- |
| A size of another shape on a transparent preset | "An export that keeps transparency has to have the canvas's own shape…". See [Transparent presets](#transparent-presets). |
| A stem's file would be one of the project's media | "The stem "…" would replace media this project uses; export under another name." |
| A graphic fails while it's drawn | "The export was stopped at frame … of the graphic "…": …. No file was written." |
| A retimed clip's sound, an isolated voice or a voice effect couldn't be rendered | The sentence names the clip and the reason. |
| A cut-out clip's masks couldn't be made | "Clip …'s person masks could not be made: …." A picture cut out by **Foreground** says foreground masks. |
| A clip's gate, leveller or de-esser needs a loudness that hasn't been measured | "Clip …'s loudness or speech has not been measured yet…". Wait for the clip's analysis, then export again. |
| This Mac has no encoder for the preset | "This Mac cannot export with the "…" preset." |

A failed export leaves no file behind. A graphic's warnings are different: they don't stop the export, and they arrive as `graphic_warnings` in the `done` answer.

## Presets

There are 15 presets, one per encoding. A preset says nothing about size. These are the rows of the sheet's **Format** control, described in [Choose a format](/export/formats/). A wrong id's error lists them all.

| Preset | In the sheet | File | Picture | Sound |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `h264` | H.264 (MP4) | `.mp4` | 8-bit. What the sheet opens on. | AAC |
| `hevc` | HEVC (MP4) | `.mp4` | 8-bit | AAC |
| `hevc_alpha` | HEVC with Alpha (MOV) | `.mov` | 8-bit with transparency. Safari's transparent movie. | AAC |
| `hevc_10bit` | HEVC 10-bit (MP4) | `.mp4` | 10-bit | AAC |
| `av1` | AV1 (MP4) | `.mp4` | 10-bit | AAC |
| `av1_webm` | AV1 (WebM) | `.webm` | 10-bit | Opus |
| `vp9_webm` | VP9 (WebM) | `.webm` | 8-bit for an SDR picture, 10-bit for HLG and PQ. One speed. | Opus |
| `vp9_alpha_webm` | VP9 with Alpha (WebM) | `.webm` | Always 8-bit, with transparency. The transparent movie Chrome and Firefox play. | Opus |
| `prores_422` | ProRes 422 (MOV) | `.mov` | 10-bit. An editing master. | 16-bit LPCM |
| `prores_4444` | ProRes 4444 (MOV) | `.mov` | 12-bit with transparency. A master. | 16-bit LPCM |
| `audio_m4a` | Audio only (M4A) | `.m4a` | None | AAC |
| `audio_wav` | Audio only (WAV) | `.wav` | None | 48 kHz LPCM, 16 or 24 bits |
| `audio_aiff` | Audio only (AIFF) | `.aiff` | None | 48 kHz LPCM, 16 or 24 bits |
| `gif` | Animated GIF | `.gif` | 256 colours. Capped at 480 × 270. | None |
| `apng` | Animated PNG | `.png` | Lossless, with transparency. Capped at 960 × 540. | None |

Macs before M3 can't play `av1` and `av1_webm` back.

## Frame rate

There's no frame-rate argument, so the sheet's [frame rate](/export/frame-rate/) control has no agent equivalent. An export runs at the project's rate, `gif` at 12.5 fps and `apng` at 25 fps. The `done` answer's `fps` says which, with 12.5 fps as `[25, 2]`.

## Path handling

The folder must exist. A `~` at the start is expanded, and an existing file at the path is replaced.

The file always ends in the preset's extension.

| `path` | `preset` | Writes | Why |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `cut.mp4` | `h264` | `cut.mp4` | The extension is already right. |
| `cut` | `h264` | `cut.mp4` | With no extension, it's added. |
| `cut.mov` | `h264` | `cut.mp4` | A different media extension is replaced. |
| `Talk v1.2` | `h264` | `Talk v1.2.mp4` | Any other suffix stays part of the name. |
| `cut.webm` | `h264` | `cut.webm.mp4` | `.webm` isn't one of the extensions Frame Job replaces. |
| `cut.mp4` | `av1_webm` | `cut.webm` | `.mp4` is. |

The extensions it replaces are `.mov`, `.mp4`, `.m4v`, `.m4a`, `.mp3`, `.wav`, `.aif`, `.aiff`, `.caf`, `.framejob`, `.srt`, `.vtt`, `.png`, `.jpg`, `.jpeg`, `.heic` and `.gif`. The answer's `path` is always the file that gets written.

## Size

`size` is the sheet's **Size** control. See [Export size](/export/size/) for what the sizes mean to a person.

| `size` | In the sheet | What it writes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `document` | Document size | The project's own size. The default on every movie preset. |
| `2160p` | 4K | A short edge of 2160 pixels. |
| `1440p` | 1440p | A short edge of 1440 pixels. |
| `1080p` | 1080p | A short edge of 1080 pixels. |
| `720p` | 720p | A short edge of 720 pixels. |
| `preset` | GIF default, APNG default | The format's cap. `gif` and `apng` only, where it's the default. |
| `[width, height]` | Custom… | Exactly this size, from 16 to 8192 pixels on each edge. |

The number is always the short edge, and the long edge follows the project's shape, rounded to an even number. A vertical project's `1080p` is 1080 × 1920. Every size means the same on every project, so a 1920 × 1080 project's `1080p` is its own size, and a size larger than the project scales it up.

A movie is written at exactly the size asked for. If the shape differs from the project's by more than a pixel, the picture is letterboxed. Within a pixel, it fills the frame instead.

- **Even edges.** Every preset but `prores_4444`, `gif` and `apng` needs even dimensions, so an odd width or height is written one pixel smaller. That covers `document` on a project with an odd edge. The `done` answer's `width` and `height` are the file's.
- **GIF and APNG.** A size is a box the picture is fitted inside, keeping its shape and never scaling up. A vertical 1080 × 1920 project's GIF default comes out at 152 × 270.
- **Audio presets.** A size has no effect, and `preset` isn't one of their sizes.
- **Transparent movies.** A `[width, height]` of another shape fails. See [Transparent presets](#transparent-presets).

An unknown size answers with the list, for example "No export size is called "480p" for h264. The sizes are: document, 2160p, 1440p, 1080p, 720p — or pass [width, height]." A custom size outside 16 to 8192 pixels is turned down the same way. Frame Job doesn't clamp it, because a tool's caller has no field to watch.

## Range

`range` is the sheet's **Range** control. `project`, the default, writes the whole timeline. `in_out` writes the range set with `set_range`, and it's turned down when there's no range. See [Export a range](/export/range/).

The range is snapped to the export's frame grid and kept inside the project. A range that comes to nothing is turned down.

`burn_in_timecode` shows project time even in a range export, so a file written from 00:00:10:00 begins at 00:00 with a burn-in that reads 00:00:10:00.

## Exact bitrates

The sheet offers [quality](/export/quality/) tiers. An agent sets the rates directly, in bits per second, so 8 Mbps is `8000000`. Each must be a whole number from 1 to 4,294,967,295.

`video_bitrate` is the target video rate. Without it, the preset's own encoder settings decide. ProRes, GIF and APNG ignore it, because ProRes is fixed by its profile and the other two have no bitrate.

On the AV1 and VP9 presets it works differently:

- **`av1` and `av1_webm`.** It's a soft cap. The encoder works at a constant quality matched to HEVC at that rate, and the file usually comes in well under it. Very detailed footage can go up to about 1.25 times over. Without it, the quality is matched to HEVC at 0.07 bits per pixel per frame.
- **`vp9_webm`.** It's a soft cap too, matched to HEVC, or HEVC 10-bit in an HDR export. Up to about 1.15 times over was measured.
- **`vp9_alpha_webm`.** It's the same soft cap on the picture's stream alone. The transparency's stream comes on top, at about 6–15 % of the video at 1080p, and up to about 39 % at 640 × 360, as measured.

`audio_bitrate` is the AAC or Opus rate, 192 kbps when absent. Opus takes the nearest rate its encoder offers. ProRes, WAV and AIFF ignore it, because they write LPCM.

## The loudness report

Every export with sound measures its own mix and reports it as `loudness` in the `done` answer, normalised or not. GIF and APNG have no sound, and a timeline with no sound has nothing to measure, so `loudness` is absent from both.

`loudness_lufs` normalises the whole mix to an integrated loudness, from −70 to 0. The sheet's [Loudness](/export/loudness/) rows are −14 for streaming, −16 for podcasts and −23 for EBU R 128 broadcast, and an agent can ask for any value, such as −14.5. The export measures itself first, then applies one gain to everything, through the master limiter. The file lands on the target with its loudest peaks limited, rather than the whole mix held down. GIF and APNG ignore it.

| Key | What it holds |
| --- | --- |
| `summary` | The same line the queue row and the progress sheet show, such as "Peak −1.0 dBTP · −16.0 LUFS", with " · peaks limited by 8.6 dB" when the limiter took 0.05 dB or more. |
| `integrated_lufs` | The file's integrated loudness. Absent when it has none, and `summary` then says "loudness not measurable". |
| `true_peak_dbtp` | The file's true peak. `null` when it's silent. |
| `sample_peak_dbfs` | The file's sample peak, never above the true peak. `null` when it's silent. |
| `gain_db` | The gain applied to reach the target. |
| `ceiling_dbtp` | The master limiter's ceiling. |
| `limited_db` | How far the limiter turned the loudest peak down. |
| `capped_by_gain` | `true` when the +40 dB limit on the gain decided it, so the file may be short of the target. |
| `target_lufs` | The `loudness_lufs` asked for. Absent when none was. |

A programme shorter than one 400 ms measuring block, or one too quiet to pass the standard's gate, has a peak and no integrated loudness. Digital silence reads "Silent" in `summary`.

## Peak dBTP

Every export with sound goes through a master limiter, so the file's true peak stays at or under a ceiling. `peak_dbtp` sets that ceiling, from −20 to 0. It's −1 when absent, which is the sheet's fixed value. 0 is the loosest, and there's no way to turn the limiter off.

You can pass it with or without `loudness_lufs`. `limited_db` in the [report](#the-loudness-report) says how far the limiter turned the loudest peak down.

## Audio bits

`audio_bits` is the sheet's [Bit depth](/export/bit-depth/) control: 16, the default, or 24. It's rounded once from the mix and never dithered, and the `done` answer repeats it.

It works on `audio_wav` and `audio_aiff` only. On any other preset the answer is "h264 has no bit depth; audio_bits applies to audio_wav and audio_aiff", naming the preset. ProRes keeps 16-bit sound. Any other number is turned down whatever the preset.

## Stems

`stems` also writes [stems](/export/stems/) beside the mix, on `audio_m4a`, `audio_wav` and `audio_aiff`. It's the sheet's **Stems** control.

| `stems` | What it writes |
| --- | --- |
| `tracks` | One file per heard track. |
| `names` | One file per track name. Heard tracks whose names match, ignoring case, share a file, and an unnamed track gets its own. |

A track is heard when it has sound in it and isn't muted or silenced by another track's solo. Each stem is named `<file> - <track name>.<ext>`, beside the mix, so `mix.wav` and a track called Voice give `mix - Voice.wav`. An unnamed track is `Track N`, `/` and `:` in a name become `-`, and two stems that would share a name are told apart with ` (Track N)`.

A stem holds its tracks' sound before the master, with no loudness gain and no limiter, so the stems add up to the mix wherever the master changed nothing. Any file already at a stem's name is replaced.

The `done` answer lists each one as `stems [{name, tracks, path}]`. `tracks` holds the ids of the timeline tracks in that stem.

- On any other preset the answer is "h264 has no stems; stems applies to audio_m4a, audio_wav and audio_aiff", naming the preset.
- With no track heard, it's "stems: no track is heard, so there is no stem to write".
- If a stem's file would be one of the project's media, the job fails before any stem is written, and `export_status` gives the reason.
- A failed or cancelled job leaves neither the mix nor any stem behind.

## Dynamic range

`dynamic_range` chooses the picture an [HLG project](/hdr/dynamic-range/) writes. It's the sheet's **Dynamic Range** control.

| `dynamic_range` | What it writes |
| --- | --- |
| `hlg` | BT.2100 HLG, with no Dolby Vision. The default on the presets that carry HDR. |
| `pq` | HDR10: BT.2100 PQ at 1,000 cd/m², with a P3-D65 mastering display of 0.005–1,000 cd/m², MaxCLL 1,000 and MaxFALL 0. |
| `sdr` | The project's SDR version. |

The presets that carry HDR are `hevc_10bit`, `av1`, `av1_webm`, `vp9_webm`, `prores_422` and `prores_4444`. Every other video preset in an HLG project writes the SDR version, `vp9_alpha_webm` included, and audio presets ignore the argument.

- `hlg` or `pq` on another video preset answers "h264 is 8-bit and writes the SDR version; export dynamic_range "pq" as hevc_10bit, av1, av1_webm, vp9_webm, prores_422 or prores_4444".
- `hlg` or `pq` in an SDR project answers "dynamic_range "pq" needs an HLG project; set_canvas output "hlg" first".
- `sdr` in an SDR project changes nothing.

Once a job is `done`, `dynamic_range` in the answer names the picture that was written. An SDR project's answer has no such key.

## Encoder speed

`encoder_speed` trades export time for file size on `av1` and `av1_webm`. It's the sheet's [Speed](/export/encoder-speed/) control, and the `done` answer names the one used.

| `encoder_speed` | SVT-AV1 preset | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `faster` | 8 | The quickest, with a larger file. |
| `balanced` | 6 | The default. |
| `smaller` | 4 | The smallest file for the picture, and the slowest. |

On every other preset the answer is "h264 has no encoder speed; encoder_speed applies to av1 and av1_webm", naming the preset. That includes `vp9_webm` and `vp9_alpha_webm`, which have one speed.

## Transparent presets

Four presets keep a transparent canvas transparent: `prores_4444`, `hevc_alpha`, `vp9_alpha_webm` and `apng`. See [Transparent exports](/export/transparency/). A GIF can show a fully transparent pixel, but it has no alpha channel, so nothing partial survives.

On the three movie presets, a `[width, height]` of a different shape from the canvas can't be written, because the padding would destroy the alpha channel. `export` queues the job, and `export_status` then reads `failed` with a reason that names both sizes. The shape is judged after an odd edge is evened, and within a pixel the picture fills the frame, so a size in the canvas's own proportions always works, at any scale. Every named size already has the canvas's shape.

`apng` fits its picture inside the size instead, so this doesn't apply to it.

---
title: "Export: start, then poll"
description: Write a file from an agent, follow the job until it finishes, stop it, and read what the file holds.
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

An agent's export doesn't wait for the file. `export` checks the request, puts a job on the Export Queue and answers at once, and the agent then asks how it's going until it ends.

<AtAGlance
  menu={['File ▸ Export…', 'Window ▸ Export Queue']}
  keys="⌘E"
  where="The export sheet's Add to Queue, and each row's Cancel in the Export Queue"
  tools={['export', 'export_status', 'cancel_export']}
/>

## Write a file

<Steps>

1. Call `export` with a preset and a path. It answers straight away.

   ```json
   { "preset": "h264", "path": "~/Movies/cut.mp4", "size": "1080p" }
   ```

   ```json
   { "export_id": 3, "path": "/Users/you/Movies/cut.mp4", "status": "running" }
   ```

2. Call `export_status` with that `export_id`, pause, and call it again until `status` is `done`, `failed` or `cancelled`.

3. Read the `done` answer. It says what the file holds, including the loudness it measured and any warnings.

</Steps>

To stop the job, call `cancel_export`. The job shows in **Window ▸ Export Queue** like any other, but the window doesn't open by itself.

## Export

`export` does what **File ▸ Export…** does with **Add to Queue**, and it runs through the same writer, so an agent's file and a person's match. It takes the [export sheet](/export/export-sheet/)'s controls in the sheet's own terms, apart from the frame rate.

| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `preset` | string | Yes | The encoding: a container and a codec. See [Presets](#presets). |
| `path` | string | Yes | Where to write, such as `~/Movies/cut.mp4`. See [Path handling](#path-handling). |
| `size` | string or `[width, height]` | No | The output size. See [Size](#size). |
| `range` | string | No | `project` for the whole timeline, or `in_out` for the in and out range. See [Range](#range). |
| `video_bitrate` | integer | No | Target video rate in bits per second. See [Exact bitrates](#exact-bitrates). |
| `audio_bitrate` | integer | No | Target AAC or Opus rate in bits per second. See [Exact bitrates](#exact-bitrates). |
| `loudness_lufs` | number | No | Normalise the whole mix to this loudness, −70 to 0. See [The loudness report](#the-loudness-report). |
| `peak_dbtp` | number | No | The master limiter's ceiling, −20 to 0. See [Peak dBTP](#peak-dbtp). |
| `audio_bits` | integer | No | 16 or 24, for WAV and AIFF. See [Audio bits](#audio-bits). |
| `stems` | string | No | `tracks` or `names`, to write stems beside an audio mix. See [Stems](#stems). |
| `burn_in_timecode` | boolean | No | Draw the project timecode over the picture, on top of everything. Off by default. See [Burn in timecode](/export/burn-in-timecode/). |
| `dynamic_range` | string | No | `hlg`, `pq` or `sdr`, in an HLG project. See [Dynamic range](#dynamic-range). |
| `encoder_speed` | string | No | `faster`, `balanced` or `smaller`, for AV1. See [Encoder speed](#encoder-speed). |
| `project` | string | No | The path of the open project to export, as `get_project` reports it. Without it, the frontmost project. |

It answers `{export_id, path, status}`. `path` is the file that will be written, with `~` expanded and the extension corrected. `status` is `running` if the job started at once, or `queued` if it's waiting.

Exports run one at a time, behind anything already in the queue. A job writes the project as it stood when `export` was called, so later edits don't reach it. Calling `export` pauses playback in that project's window.

`export` takes no `scope`. With a [nest](/mcp/nests/) open it still writes the project's timeline, not the nest's.

## Export status

`export_status` answers how a job is going, as its row in the Export Queue would, and it never waits. Pass the `export_id`, which is an integer of 1 or more.

Every answer carries `export_id`, `status`, `path` and `elapsed`, the seconds since `export` was called, or from then to the finish once the job has ended. The rest depends on the status.

| `status` | Also carries |
| --- | --- |
| `queued` | `waiting` while an AV1 or VP9 job is held for memory. `estimated_seconds` on `av1`, `av1_webm`, `vp9_webm` and `vp9_alpha_webm`. |
| `running` | `progress`, from 0 to 1. `phase` while the export names one, which is "Measuring loudness…" during the first pass over the mix. `estimated_seconds` on the same four presets. |
| `done` | What the file holds, in the next table. |
| `failed` | `reason`, the queue row's sentence. |
| `cancelled` | `reason`, the queue row's sentence. |

`estimated_seconds` is the export sheet's estimate of the whole export in whole seconds, and it's only an estimate.

`waiting` is a sentence such as "Waiting for memory: AV1 and VP9 exports running now hold about 2.1 GB of the 8.0 GB this Mac allows them, and this one needs about 7.0 GB." AV1 and VP9 exports may hold a quarter of this Mac's memory between them. While one is held, a later job in the queue may run first.

A `done` answer adds these keys.

| Key | What it holds |
| --- | --- |
| `ok` | `true`. |
| `bytes` | The file's size. |
| `preset`, `container`, `codec` | What was written. |
| `width`, `height` | The file's size in pixels. These are reported on audio presets too, where they mean nothing. |
| `fps` | The rate as `[num, den]`, such as `[30, 1]`. |
| `start`, `duration` | The part of the timeline written, in [ticks](/mcp/units-and-ids/). |
| `burn_in_timecode` | Whether the argument was on. |
| `dynamic_range` | The picture written: `hlg`, `pq` or `sdr`. Only for a video preset in an HLG project. |
| `encoder_speed` | The speed used. Only on `av1` and `av1_webm`. |
| `audio_bits` | The depth written. Only on `audio_wav` and `audio_aiff`. |
| `stems` | `[{name, tracks, path}]`, one per file beside the mix. Only when `stems` was asked for. |
| `loudness` | What the mix measured. See [The loudness report](#the-loudness-report). |
| `graphic_warnings` | `[{name, frame, message}]`, each distinct warning a graphic gave while the file was drawn, up to 64. `frame` is the graphic's own frame, or `null`. Absent when there were none. |
| `cursor_warnings` | `[{media, path, message}]`, each media whose cursor file couldn't be drawn. Its clips were written without a cursor. Absent when there were none. |

## Cancel export

`cancel_export` stops a job, as the row's **Cancel** does, and answers as `export_status` does. Pass the `export_id`.

| The job is | What happens |
| --- | --- |
| Queued | It's cancelled before it starts. The answer reads `cancelled`, with the reason "Cancelled before it started." |
| Running | It stops and its half-written file is removed. The answer may still read `running` until the writer has stopped, and `export_status` then reads `cancelled`, with the reason "Cancelled." |
| Finished | It's left alone, and its file stays. The answer is the finished job's. |

## Export id and its lifetime

An `export_id` is known until Frame Job quits. Removing a finished row from the Export Queue, or choosing **Clear Finished**, doesn't lose it, so an agent can still read how that job ended.

Only ids that `export` answered are known. A job a person queued from the sheet has no id an agent can follow. Any other number answers "No export this launch has export_id 7 — ids come from export and last until Frame Job quits."

## Refusals and failures

A problem Frame Job can see from the request comes back from `export` itself as an error, and nothing is queued.

| The request | What stops it |
| --- | --- |
| An empty timeline | "There is nothing on the timeline to export." |
| A folder that doesn't exist | "There is no folder at … to write into." Frame Job never creates the folder. |
| An unknown preset | The error lists all the presets. |
| An unknown `size`, or one it can't read | The error lists the sizes. See [Size](#size). |
| `range` of `in_out` with no range set | "This project has no in/out range — set one with set_range `{start, end}`, or export with range \"project\"." |
| A number out of range, or a word it doesn't know | The error names the argument and the value. |
| An option the preset doesn't have | See [Audio bits](#audio-bits), [Stems](#stems), [Dynamic range](#dynamic-range) and [Encoder speed](#encoder-speed). |
| A graphic clip in the range with no module, or a module that doesn't compile | "The export was not started: the graphic "…" does not compile — …. Fix the module and export again." It names each graphic and its first error, and it covers graphics inside nests. An audio-only preset draws no graphics, so it isn't stopped by one. |

Anything that goes wrong after that comes back from `export_status` as `failed`, with the sentence in `reason`. Check for it even when `export` answered cleanly.

| What went wrong | The `reason` |
| --- | --- |
| A size of another shape on a transparent preset | "An export that keeps transparency has to have the canvas's own shape…". See [Transparent presets](#transparent-presets). |
| A stem's file would be one of the project's media | "The stem "…" would replace media this project uses; export under another name." |
| A graphic fails while it's drawn | "The export was stopped at frame … of the graphic "…": …. No file was written." |
| A retimed clip's sound, an isolated voice or a voice effect couldn't be rendered | The sentence names the clip and the reason. |
| A cut-out clip's masks couldn't be made | "Clip …'s person masks could not be made: …." A picture cut out by **Foreground** says foreground masks. |
| A clip's gate, leveller or de-esser needs a loudness that hasn't been measured | "Clip …'s loudness or speech has not been measured yet…". Wait for the clip's analysis, then export again. |
| This Mac has no encoder for the preset | "This Mac cannot export with the "…" preset." |

A failed export leaves no file behind. A graphic's warnings are different: they don't stop the export, and they arrive as `graphic_warnings` in the `done` answer.

## Presets

There are 15 presets, one per encoding. A preset says nothing about size. These are the rows of the sheet's **Format** control, described in [Choose a format](/export/formats/). A wrong id's error lists them all.

| Preset | In the sheet | File | Picture | Sound |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `h264` | H.264 (MP4) | `.mp4` | 8-bit. What the sheet opens on. | AAC |
| `hevc` | HEVC (MP4) | `.mp4` | 8-bit | AAC |
| `hevc_alpha` | HEVC with Alpha (MOV) | `.mov` | 8-bit with transparency. Safari's transparent movie. | AAC |
| `hevc_10bit` | HEVC 10-bit (MP4) | `.mp4` | 10-bit | AAC |
| `av1` | AV1 (MP4) | `.mp4` | 10-bit | AAC |
| `av1_webm` | AV1 (WebM) | `.webm` | 10-bit | Opus |
| `vp9_webm` | VP9 (WebM) | `.webm` | 8-bit for an SDR picture, 10-bit for HLG and PQ. One speed. | Opus |
| `vp9_alpha_webm` | VP9 with Alpha (WebM) | `.webm` | Always 8-bit, with transparency. The transparent movie Chrome and Firefox play. | Opus |
| `prores_422` | ProRes 422 (MOV) | `.mov` | 10-bit. An editing master. | 16-bit LPCM |
| `prores_4444` | ProRes 4444 (MOV) | `.mov` | 12-bit with transparency. A master. | 16-bit LPCM |
| `audio_m4a` | Audio only (M4A) | `.m4a` | None | AAC |
| `audio_wav` | Audio only (WAV) | `.wav` | None | 48 kHz LPCM, 16 or 24 bits |
| `audio_aiff` | Audio only (AIFF) | `.aiff` | None | 48 kHz LPCM, 16 or 24 bits |
| `gif` | Animated GIF | `.gif` | 256 colours. Capped at 480 × 270. | None |
| `apng` | Animated PNG | `.png` | Lossless, with transparency. Capped at 960 × 540. | None |

Macs before M3 can't play `av1` and `av1_webm` back.

## Frame rate

There's no frame-rate argument, so the sheet's [frame rate](/export/frame-rate/) control has no agent equivalent. An export runs at the project's rate, `gif` at 12.5 fps and `apng` at 25 fps. The `done` answer's `fps` says which, with 12.5 fps as `[25, 2]`.

## Path handling

The folder must exist. A `~` at the start is expanded, and an existing file at the path is replaced.

The file always ends in the preset's extension.

| `path` | `preset` | Writes | Why |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `cut.mp4` | `h264` | `cut.mp4` | The extension is already right. |
| `cut` | `h264` | `cut.mp4` | With no extension, it's added. |
| `cut.mov` | `h264` | `cut.mp4` | A different media extension is replaced. |
| `Talk v1.2` | `h264` | `Talk v1.2.mp4` | Any other suffix stays part of the name. |
| `cut.webm` | `h264` | `cut.webm.mp4` | `.webm` isn't one of the extensions Frame Job replaces. |
| `cut.mp4` | `av1_webm` | `cut.webm` | `.mp4` is. |

The extensions it replaces are `.mov`, `.mp4`, `.m4v`, `.m4a`, `.mp3`, `.wav`, `.aif`, `.aiff`, `.caf`, `.framejob`, `.srt`, `.vtt`, `.png`, `.jpg`, `.jpeg`, `.heic` and `.gif`. The answer's `path` is always the file that gets written.

## Size

`size` is the sheet's **Size** control. See [Export size](/export/size/) for what the sizes mean to a person.

| `size` | In the sheet | What it writes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `document` | Document size | The project's own size. The default on every movie preset. |
| `2160p` | 4K | A short edge of 2160 pixels. |
| `1440p` | 1440p | A short edge of 1440 pixels. |
| `1080p` | 1080p | A short edge of 1080 pixels. |
| `720p` | 720p | A short edge of 720 pixels. |
| `preset` | GIF default, APNG default | The format's cap. `gif` and `apng` only, where it's the default. |
| `[width, height]` | Custom… | Exactly this size, from 16 to 8192 pixels on each edge. |

The number is always the short edge, and the long edge follows the project's shape, rounded to an even number. A vertical project's `1080p` is 1080 × 1920. Every size means the same on every project, so a 1920 × 1080 project's `1080p` is its own size, and a size larger than the project scales it up.

A movie is written at exactly the size asked for. If the shape differs from the project's by more than a pixel, the picture is letterboxed. Within a pixel, it fills the frame instead.

- **Even edges.** Every preset but `prores_4444`, `gif` and `apng` needs even dimensions, so an odd width or height is written one pixel smaller. That covers `document` on a project with an odd edge. The `done` answer's `width` and `height` are the file's.
- **GIF and APNG.** A size is a box the picture is fitted inside, keeping its shape and never scaling up. A vertical 1080 × 1920 project's GIF default comes out at 152 × 270.
- **Audio presets.** A size has no effect, and `preset` isn't one of their sizes.
- **Transparent movies.** A `[width, height]` of another shape fails. See [Transparent presets](#transparent-presets).

An unknown size answers with the list, for example "No export size is called "480p" for h264. The sizes are: document, 2160p, 1440p, 1080p, 720p — or pass [width, height]." A custom size outside 16 to 8192 pixels is turned down the same way. Frame Job doesn't clamp it, because a tool's caller has no field to watch.

## Range

`range` is the sheet's **Range** control. `project`, the default, writes the whole timeline. `in_out` writes the range set with `set_range`, and it's turned down when there's no range. See [Export a range](/export/range/).

The range is snapped to the export's frame grid and kept inside the project. A range that comes to nothing is turned down.

`burn_in_timecode` shows project time even in a range export, so a file written from 00:00:10:00 begins at 00:00 with a burn-in that reads 00:00:10:00.

## Exact bitrates

The sheet offers [quality](/export/quality/) tiers. An agent sets the rates directly, in bits per second, so 8 Mbps is `8000000`. Each must be a whole number from 1 to 4,294,967,295.

`video_bitrate` is the target video rate. Without it, the preset's own encoder settings decide. ProRes, GIF and APNG ignore it, because ProRes is fixed by its profile and the other two have no bitrate.

On the AV1 and VP9 presets it works differently:

- **`av1` and `av1_webm`.** It's a soft cap. The encoder works at a constant quality matched to HEVC at that rate, and the file usually comes in well under it. Very detailed footage can go up to about 1.25 times over. Without it, the quality is matched to HEVC at 0.07 bits per pixel per frame.
- **`vp9_webm`.** It's a soft cap too, matched to HEVC, or HEVC 10-bit in an HDR export. Up to about 1.15 times over was measured.
- **`vp9_alpha_webm`.** It's the same soft cap on the picture's stream alone. The transparency's stream comes on top, at about 6–15 % of the video at 1080p, and up to about 39 % at 640 × 360, as measured.

`audio_bitrate` is the AAC or Opus rate, 192 kbps when absent. Opus takes the nearest rate its encoder offers. ProRes, WAV and AIFF ignore it, because they write LPCM.

## The loudness report

Every export with sound measures its own mix and reports it as `loudness` in the `done` answer, normalised or not. GIF and APNG have no sound, and a timeline with no sound has nothing to measure, so `loudness` is absent from both.

`loudness_lufs` normalises the whole mix to an integrated loudness, from −70 to 0. The sheet's [Loudness](/export/loudness/) rows are −14 for streaming, −16 for podcasts and −23 for EBU R 128 broadcast, and an agent can ask for any value, such as −14.5. The export measures itself first, then applies one gain to everything, through the master limiter. The file lands on the target with its loudest peaks limited, rather than the whole mix held down. GIF and APNG ignore it.

| Key | What it holds |
| --- | --- |
| `summary` | The same line the queue row and the progress sheet show, such as "Peak −1.0 dBTP · −16.0 LUFS", with " · peaks limited by 8.6 dB" when the limiter took 0.05 dB or more. |
| `integrated_lufs` | The file's integrated loudness. Absent when it has none, and `summary` then says "loudness not measurable". |
| `true_peak_dbtp` | The file's true peak. `null` when it's silent. |
| `sample_peak_dbfs` | The file's sample peak, never above the true peak. `null` when it's silent. |
| `gain_db` | The gain applied to reach the target. |
| `ceiling_dbtp` | The master limiter's ceiling. |
| `limited_db` | How far the limiter turned the loudest peak down. |
| `capped_by_gain` | `true` when the +40 dB limit on the gain decided it, so the file may be short of the target. |
| `target_lufs` | The `loudness_lufs` asked for. Absent when none was. |

A programme shorter than one 400 ms measuring block, or one too quiet to pass the standard's gate, has a peak and no integrated loudness. Digital silence reads "Silent" in `summary`.

## Peak dBTP

Every export with sound goes through a master limiter, so the file's true peak stays at or under a ceiling. `peak_dbtp` sets that ceiling, from −20 to 0. It's −1 when absent, which is the sheet's fixed value. 0 is the loosest, and there's no way to turn the limiter off.

You can pass it with or without `loudness_lufs`. `limited_db` in the [report](#the-loudness-report) says how far the limiter turned the loudest peak down.

## Audio bits

`audio_bits` is the sheet's [Bit depth](/export/bit-depth/) control: 16, the default, or 24. It's rounded once from the mix and never dithered, and the `done` answer repeats it.

It works on `audio_wav` and `audio_aiff` only. On any other preset the answer is "h264 has no bit depth; audio_bits applies to audio_wav and audio_aiff", naming the preset. ProRes keeps 16-bit sound. Any other number is turned down whatever the preset.

## Stems

`stems` also writes [stems](/export/stems/) beside the mix, on `audio_m4a`, `audio_wav` and `audio_aiff`. It's the sheet's **Stems** control.

| `stems` | What it writes |
| --- | --- |
| `tracks` | One file per heard track. |
| `names` | One file per track name. Heard tracks whose names match, ignoring case, share a file, and an unnamed track gets its own. |

A track is heard when it has sound in it and isn't muted or silenced by another track's solo. Each stem is named `<file> - <track name>.<ext>`, beside the mix, so `mix.wav` and a track called Voice give `mix - Voice.wav`. An unnamed track is `Track N`, `/` and `:` in a name become `-`, and two stems that would share a name are told apart with ` (Track N)`.

A stem holds its tracks' sound before the master, with no loudness gain and no limiter, so the stems add up to the mix wherever the master changed nothing. Any file already at a stem's name is replaced.

The `done` answer lists each one as `stems [{name, tracks, path}]`. `tracks` holds the ids of the timeline tracks in that stem.

- On any other preset the answer is "h264 has no stems; stems applies to audio_m4a, audio_wav and audio_aiff", naming the preset.
- With no track heard, it's "stems: no track is heard, so there is no stem to write".
- If a stem's file would be one of the project's media, the job fails before any stem is written, and `export_status` gives the reason.
- A failed or cancelled job leaves neither the mix nor any stem behind.

## Dynamic range

`dynamic_range` chooses the picture an [HLG project](/hdr/dynamic-range/) writes. It's the sheet's **Dynamic Range** control.

| `dynamic_range` | What it writes |
| --- | --- |
| `hlg` | BT.2100 HLG, with no Dolby Vision. The default on the presets that carry HDR. |
| `pq` | HDR10: BT.2100 PQ at 1,000 cd/m², with a P3-D65 mastering display of 0.005–1,000 cd/m², MaxCLL 1,000 and MaxFALL 0. |
| `sdr` | The project's SDR version. |

The presets that carry HDR are `hevc_10bit`, `av1`, `av1_webm`, `vp9_webm`, `prores_422` and `prores_4444`. Every other video preset in an HLG project writes the SDR version, `vp9_alpha_webm` included, and audio presets ignore the argument.

- `hlg` or `pq` on another video preset answers "h264 is 8-bit and writes the SDR version; export dynamic_range "pq" as hevc_10bit, av1, av1_webm, vp9_webm, prores_422 or prores_4444".
- `hlg` or `pq` in an SDR project answers "dynamic_range "pq" needs an HLG project; set_canvas output "hlg" first".
- `sdr` in an SDR project changes nothing.

Once a job is `done`, `dynamic_range` in the answer names the picture that was written. An SDR project's answer has no such key.

## Encoder speed

`encoder_speed` trades export time for file size on `av1` and `av1_webm`. It's the sheet's [Speed](/export/encoder-speed/) control, and the `done` answer names the one used.

| `encoder_speed` | SVT-AV1 preset | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `faster` | 8 | The quickest, with a larger file. |
| `balanced` | 6 | The default. |
| `smaller` | 4 | The smallest file for the picture, and the slowest. |

On every other preset the answer is "h264 has no encoder speed; encoder_speed applies to av1 and av1_webm", naming the preset. That includes `vp9_webm` and `vp9_alpha_webm`, which have one speed.

## Transparent presets

Four presets keep a transparent canvas transparent: `prores_4444`, `hevc_alpha`, `vp9_alpha_webm` and `apng`. See [Transparent exports](/export/transparency/). A GIF can show a fully transparent pixel, but it has no alpha channel, so nothing partial survives.

On the three movie presets, a `[width, height]` of a different shape from the canvas can't be written, because the padding would destroy the alpha channel. `export` queues the job, and `export_status` then reads `failed` with a reason that names both sizes. The shape is judged after an odd edge is evened, and within a pixel the picture fills the frame, so a size in the canvas's own proportions always works, at any scale. Every named size already has the canvas's shape.

`apng` fits its picture inside the size instead, so this doesn't apply to it.

## Related

- [The export sheet](/export/export-sheet/)
- [The Export Queue](/export/export-queue/)
- [Tools: rendering and export](/mcp/tools-render-and-export/)
- [Check the picture: render_frame](/mcp/render-frame/)
- [What a call answers](/mcp/what-a-call-answers/)

content.content:
# CLAUDE.md — the documentation site

The public user documentation: Astro with Starlight, one page per feature or tight family of
features. `pnpm` manages it, Node is pinned by `.node-version`. `README.md` has the commands.

## Where things are

```
astro.config.mjs        Starlight's settings: title, logo, fonts, theme, plugins
sidebar.mjs             every page's place in the navigation, in order
src/content/docs/       the pages: <section>/<page>.mdx
src/data/features.json  THE FEATURE LIST: what /features/ renders and what the proof reads
src/components/         AtAGlance (a page's facts), Shot (a screen in both looks),
                        FeatureIndex (the filterable list)
src/assets/screens/     WebP captures, written only by scripts/import-screens.mjs
src/styles/             the brand: the mark's inks, the app's faces, square chrome
```

## The rule that matters

**Every claim is written from the code.** A label, a default, a range, a shortcut, a limit or a
refusal is checked against `app/Sources/`, `core/src/`, `graphic/` or `mcp-proxy/` before it is
written, and the code wins over `docs/guide/`, a spec or an ADR. Never write what a feature
probably does. If the code cannot settle it, leave it out.

Nothing dev-only, deferred or unbuilt is documented. That excludes the dev tools (`snapshot_ui`,
`perform_menu_item`, `cancel_sheet`, `select_inspector_tab`, `play_preview`, `graphic_memory`,
`loudness_meter`, `land_recording`, `analysis_job`, `transcript_view`, `playback_rebuilds`,
`assistant_send`, `assistant_answer`) and every `-RCDev` launch default.

## Who reads this

Someone editing a video, who has never read this repository. They want to know what a thing does,
how to do it, and what will stop them. They do not care how it is built.

So a page never mentions: spec or decision IDs (`AU-12`, `§11`), road maps, phases, issue numbers,
source file or type names, `rc_*` exports, format version numbers, proofs, tests, or the history
of a feature. Internal words get translated: "refused" becomes what the user sees ("Frame Job
won't do this while…"), "the core" and "the op" disappear. A tool name is the one exception: the
MCP pages and `tools=` in `AtAGlance` name agent tools, because those are the product's interface.

## Voice

- Plain, direct and second person. Say what it does, then how. Short sentences.
- Open with what the feature is for, in a sentence or two, before any steps.
- British spelling in prose, as `docs/guide/` does (colour, centre, grey, normalise), and the
  app's exact spelling for its own labels (the **Color** tab, **Normalize**).
- Contractions are fine. No marketing: never "powerful", "seamless", "effortless", "robust",
  "simply", "just", "easily", "unleash", "supercharge".
- Prefer a full stop or a comma to an em dash.
- State defaults, ranges and limits as numbers. Say what happens at the edges, because that is
  what a reader comes to a reference for.
- No filler sections. A page with nothing to say under a heading doesn't have that heading.

## Page shape

```mdx
---
title: Markers
description: One sentence, what this page helps you do. Search results show it.
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';

What the feature is for, in a sentence or two.

<AtAGlance menu="Mark ▸ Add Marker" keys="M" tools="add_marker" />

<Shot name="04-editor.window" alt="What the picture shows, for someone who can't see it." />

## Add a marker

<Steps>

1. Move the playhead to the moment.
2. Press <kbd>M</kbd>.

</Steps>

## Options

| Control | What it does | Default |
| ------- | ------------ | ------- |

## Good to know

Limits, edge cases and what stops it, in plain words.

## Related

- [Snapping](/timeline/snapping/)
```

Every section is optional except the opening. Order the task sections as a reader needs them.

- **Headings** start at `##`, are sentence case, and name the job: "Add a marker", not "Adding".
  A feature in `src/data/features.json` with an `anchor` needs a heading that makes that anchor.
- **Menus** are bold with `▸`, spelled as the app spells them: **Clip ▸ Split**.
- **Keys** use the app's symbols in `<kbd>`: <kbd>⌘T</kbd>. Inside `AtAGlance`, pass the string.
- **Controls** are bold where they appear in a step: choose **Save**.
- **Links** are root-absolute with a trailing slash: `/timeline/markers/#add-a-marker`. The build
  fails on a link or anchor that does not exist.
- **Asides** are for what a reader must not miss, not for decoration: `:::note`, `:::tip`,
  `:::caution`, `:::danger`.
- **Screens** come from `src/assets/screens/`. A `name` is the file name without its look and
  extension. Use a screen only when it shows what the page is about, not when the thing is out
  of frame, and give it real alt text.

## MDX traps

MDX is JSX. In prose, `{`, `}` and `<` start code. Put anything like `{x}`, `<1 s` or `a<b` in a
code span, or write it out ("under 1 s"). `<kbd>` and every component must close. A line starting
with `import` or `export` is code. Leave a blank line after an opening component tag and before
its closing tag, or the Markdown inside won't render.

## Checking a page

```sh
node docs/site/scripts/check-pages.mjs <page.mdx>…        # parses, imports, links, captures
python3 tools/proof/docs_site_proof.py --pages <page.mdx>…  # internal words, local paths
pnpm build                                                # in docs/site: the last word
```

## Screens

The captures come from the screen catalog (`designs/screens/`, `tools/proof/screens.py`), so the
pictures are of the real app. To refresh them:

```sh
python3 tools/proof/screens.py --out <dir>                      # from the repository root
node docs/site/scripts/import-screens.mjs <dir> --used
```

**This site is public.** `import-screens.mjs` refuses a capture whose layout dump holds a local
path, and its `CROP` table is the only way past that, by cutting the region away. Settings needs
it: its MCP section prints the helper's full path. Never weaken the refusal.

## When the app changes

A user-visible change edits its page here as well as `docs/guide/`, and a new feature adds its row
to `src/data/features.json`. `tools/proof/docs_site_proof.py` runs in `make test` and fails on a
menu item or agent tool the site doesn't document, a feature whose page or anchor is missing, or a
page that names something internal.
